propositions: The comment-hygiene gate runs in CI as a standalone step but is not wired into `make lint`, causing local lint to return clean verdicts that CI rejects.
The gate's test runs only in the full pytest suite, not in the fast local lint path, preventing early detection of comment-hygiene violations before CI.
Adding the gate to `make lint` increases local lint runtime from 17.8s to ~22.7s (~4.9s overhead), which is acceptable relative to the 15-minute CI cycle cost of a miss.

The introducing ticket shows no deliberate intent to exclude the gate from `make lint`; the gate follows the scripts/check_*.py convention and mirrors the precedent set by gen_env_registry.py --check.
Wiring the gate into `make lint` while keeping the standalone CI step mirrors the env-registry drift-gate pattern and ensures local verdicts agree with CI.
